args.message: Fix money rounding to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

files.content:
"""Money rounding utilities."""

from decimal import localcontext
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_EVEN


def round_money(amount: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """Round to cents using banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN), per FIN-212."""
    # Use exact decimal arithmetic (never float) so 2.675 stays exact
    # instead of becoming 2.674999... like it would with float inputs.
    with localcontext() as ctx:
        ctx.rounding = ROUND_HALF_EVEN
        ctx.prec = 50
        return amount.quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN)

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix money rounding to banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
Nightly build was failing because tests/test_money.py expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212) but src/money.py implemented ROUND_HALF_UP despite the docstring claiming otherwise.

Fix on fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding:

- Replace ROUND_HALF_UP with ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money(), matching the existing docstring and the FIN-212 requirement.
- Keep quantize at the cents level (Decimal("0.01")) — behavior for non-half-way values is unchanged; only halfway cases (e.g. 2.665 → 2.66) now round to even.
- Also add a localcontext guard so that if callers ever pass non-Decimal/float-based values that get converted, they aren't silently rounded under a different ambient context precision.

CI run ci-0001 passed on sha f08a1e0b6f.
